name: AM2320 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Aosong digital temperature (-40 to 80 °C, ±0.5 °C) and relative humidity (0–99.9 %, ±3 %) sensor with an I2C (Modbus-style, CRC-16) interface, 0.1 unit resolution. Runs on 3.1–5.5 V; I2C up to 100 kHz; no pull-ups inside. Sold as: Adafruit AM2320 Digital Temperature and Humidity Sensor (product 3721, bare 4-lead 2.54 mm sensor: VDD, SDA, GND, SCL), fixed I2C address 0x5C (0xB8 in 8-bit notation).
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 3.1–5.5 V; use 3.3 V with ESP32/Pico so the I2C pull-ups go to 3.3 V

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data; needs an external pull-up (3–10 kΩ, e.g. 4.7 kΩ) to VDD

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock; needs an external pull-up (3–10 kΩ, e.g. 4.7 kΩ) to VDD. Held low at power-up, it selects the single-bus (DHT-style) mode instead

buildNotes: Pins, looking at the slotted front, left to right: VDD, SDA, GND, SCL. The sensor has no pull-ups: fit 3–10 kΩ (e.g. 4.7 kΩ) from SDA and from SCL to VDD.
The sensor sleeps between reads: wake it by sending its address (it does NOT acknowledge, so expect an OSError), then within 3 ms write 0x03 0x00 0x04, wait at least 1.5 ms and read 8 bytes.
Reply: 0x03, 0x04, humidity (×10), temperature (bit 15 = sign, bits 14–0 = |T| ×10), CRC-16/Modbus low byte first. A CRC or header mismatch usually means a loose wire or missing pull-ups.
Run the I2C bus at 100 kHz or slower and read at most once every 2 s; each read returns the measurement triggered by the previous read.
The address is fixed at 0x5C, so only one AM2320 can share a bus.

driver.code:
# AM2320 temperature & humidity sensor (Aosong AM2320), MicroPython driver for its I2C mode.
# Datasheet sequence: wake the sensor (address byte, which it does NOT acknowledge), send
# function 0x03 "read registers" from 0x00 for 4 registers, wait >= 1.5 ms, then read
# 8 bytes: 0x03, 0x04, RH high, RH low, T high, T low, CRC low, CRC high.
# CRC-16/Modbus (init 0xFFFF, poly 0xA001 reflected) over the first 6 bytes, sent low byte first.
# Humidity = raw / 10 %RH. Temperature: bit 15 = sign (1 = negative), bits 14..0 = |T| x 10.
# Bus speed must be 100 kHz or less. Read no more often than once every 2 s.
import time

ADDR = 0x5C  # 0xB8 in the datasheet's 8-bit (address + R/W) notation


def _crc16(data):
    crc = 0xFFFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = (crc >> 1) ^ 0xA001 if crc & 1 else crc >> 1
    return crc


class AM2320:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def _wake(self):
        # The sensor sleeps between reads and does not ACK the wake-up address byte,
        # so the write normally raises OSError: that is expected.
        try:
            self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'')
        except OSError:
            pass
        time.sleep_ms(1)  # datasheet: hold >= 800 us (max 3 ms) before it is awake

    def read(self):
        """Return (temperature in °C, relative humidity in %).

        The sensor starts a new measurement each time it is read, so a reading
        reflects the previous read; wait at least 2 s between calls.
        """
        self._wake()
        try:
            self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x03\x00\x04')
        except OSError:
            # Some ports need a second attempt right after waking the sensor.
            time.sleep_ms(1)
            self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x03\x00\x04')
        time.sleep_ms(2)  # datasheet: wait at least 1.5 ms before reading
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 8)
        if d[0] != 0x03 or d[1] != 0x04:
            raise OSError('AM2320 bad reply header: check the wiring and pull-ups')
        if _crc16(d[0:6]) != (d[6] | (d[7] << 8)):
            raise OSError('AM2320 CRC mismatch: check the wiring and pull-ups')
        h_raw = (d[2] << 8) | d[3]
        t_raw = (d[4] << 8) | d[5]
        t = (t_raw & 0x7FFF) / 10
        if t_raw & 0x8000:
            t = -t
        return t, h_raw / 10

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def humidity(self):
        return self.read()[1]

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from am2320 import AM2320

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = AM2320(i2c)
while True:
    try:
        t, h = sensor.read()
        print('T=%.1fC H=%.1f%%' % (t, h))
    except OSError as e:
        print('AM2320 error:', e)
    time.sleep(2)
